A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same HSPI work. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable, and retained experiments can be matched across the substantial reformatting and relocation.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix A report original experiments involving vision models, LLMs, quantization formats, and GPU identification.

after.justification: The original empirical results remain, supplemented by SGLang serving, distributed and cross-vendor hardware experiments, and label-merging results in Section 6 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The core PGD border-input and SVM logit-distribution methods remain. Section 6.2 and Appendix D.3 add an adaptation that merges software configurations into GPU-only labels and trains a new classifier, changing the prediction target. Section 4.4 largely reorganizes model-specific adaptations already described in v1.

E1.justification: Coverage expands from direct model-inference experiments on NVIDIA hardware to optimized SGLang cloud serving and distributed, cross-vendor environments, including AMD MI300X and Amazon Inferentia. These additions substantially broaden the serving conditions and target hardware population; the original vision and random-word language tasks remain.

E2.justification: The HSPI-BI, HSPI-LD, and random-guess comparisons are retained without adding an evaluated external fingerprinting method. SGLang is a serving environment, vLLM is cited context, and the additional hardware configurations are identification targets rather than competing methods.

E3.justification: New protocols include 16-way GPU/precision/kernel/sharding classification in Table 6, distributed Llama-3.1-70B configurations in Table 10, and two-class merged-label evaluation in Table 12. Separately, v1 Table 1's RTX8000/H100 condition becomes RTX8000/A100 in v2 Table 8, although Section 5.2 still names H100. This is a reported setting inconsistency, not evidence establishing a rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix D.3 newly tests whether merging software labels preserves GPU identification using the same samples as Table 6. The original batch-size and iteration sensitivity plots remain as Figure 7, while v1's illustrative DistillGPT2 border-request case in Figure 7 is removed. Proposed noise and bit-flip mitigations remain untested discussion.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed-based uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional result tables retain this reporting practice.

E6.justification: The numerical values in v1 Tables 2–6 and Appendix A.2 are retained after renumbering. New v2 Tables 6, 10, and 11 report average accuracies of 0.991, 0.973, and 0.964, respectively; Table 12 reports 0.985 accuracy and F1. These are results under new conditions or prediction targets, not improvements over the retained 0.839 result under identical settings. The original DistillGPT2 response example is removed.

T1.justification: The access assumptions, equivalence-class concept, and mathematical content of Equations (1)–(6) remain. The newly explicit N(N−1)/2 classifier count explains the existing pairwise construction rather than introducing a substantive formal derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the HSPI identification objective and the two proposed methods. The headline claims of 83.9%–100% white-box accuracy and up to three times random-guess performance in black-box settings remain; the new experiments primarily broaden their supporting evidence.

C2.justification: Sections 6.1–6.2 add interpretations concerning applicability to optimized serving, label merging as a scalability solution, and acceptable query costs. Section 4.4 also explains random-word prompting as encouraging closer top-k logits and avoiding negative infinity. Existing equivalence-class, batch-size, and black-box limitations largely survive in Appendices E–F.

D1.justification: Appendix B.2 substantially expands the previously underspecified LLM sampling pipeline: prompt template, NLTK word source, three versus eight leading words, 256 queries per class, top-256 logits, and four responses per SVM sample. New tables specify device counts and parallelism configurations. The abstract advertises a code repository, although the conclusion still promises future code and logit-data release. These disclosures do not establish changes to the original experiments.

R1.justification: Appendix A adds explicit positioning against the side-channel work of Hua et al. and Gongye et al.; serving-framework and pricing citations are also added. The training-variability discussion and its Pham, Zhuang, and Alahmari references are removed, along with several convolution-background references. The central relationship to prior numerical fingerprinting work remains.

P1.justification: Background and methodology prose are extensively condensed and reorganized. A model-specific adaptation subsection is created, detailed settings move into Appendix B, limitations and robustness move into Appendices E–F, and much of the governance discussion moves into an Impact Statement. The discussion is substantially restructured around serving, scalability, and cost.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a two-column conference paper, with widespread resizing and relocation of figures and tables. New displays include the summary matrix, Tables 6 and 10–12, and the prompt-template Figure 8. The original DistillGPT2 figure is removed, and the fine-tuning hyperparameter table becomes prose.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses an important validation gap between v1's practical serving motivation and its simpler NVIDIA experiments. SGLang, distributed-model, and cross-vendor evaluations substantially strengthen deployment relevance, while label-merging evidence and detailed sampling instructions improve practical usability and reproducibility. The H100/A100 inconsistency and conflicting release statements are limited drawbacks. The additions remain principally white-box evidence and do not resolve the retained black-box limitations.
